chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'mar) from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Al-Husayn ibn Saif from Muhammad ibn Aslam from Muhammad ibn Sulayman who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the Hajj of Islam (his first obligatory Hajj), entering into Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break), and Allah enabled him to complete his Umrah and Hajj. Then he went to Medina, offered salams to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), then came to you, acknowledging your right, knowing that you are the proof of Allah upon His creation and the door through which one is approached. He offered salams to you, then went to Abu Abdillah Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and offered salams to him, then went to Baghdad and offered salams to Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him). Then he returned to his land. When the time for Hajj came, Allah granted him the means to perform Hajj. Which is better for this man who has already performed the Hajj of Islam: that he returns again and performs Hajj, or that he goes to Khorasan to your father - Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him) and offers salams to him? He said: 'He goes to Khorasan and offers salams to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), that is better. And let that be in Rajab, and it is not fitting that you do this on this day, for there is a danger from the Sultan upon us and upon you.'

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed by a Muslim
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khorasan, a region where Imam Ali ibn Musa was residing
key_terms.رَجَبٍ: The seventh month of the Islamic calendar
key_terms.شُنْعَةً: Danger or peril, specifically from the ruling authority
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: A state of combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between

ai.seo_question: Which is more virtuous: performing an additional Hajj or visiting the Imam in Khorasan?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the superiority of visiting the Imam (Ziyarat al-Imam) over a second Hajj, emphasizing the spiritual merit of recognizing the Imam as God's proof (Hujjah) on earth. He specifically recommends performing this visit in Rajab, a month of significant religious observance, while contextualizing the ruling within the political climate of the Abbasid era, where the 'shun'ah' (fear or danger) from the ruling authority made such pilgrimages potentially perilous yet spiritually rewarding.
